Quarantine: the four ideal Euler-Bernoulli deflection formulas match independent fixtures, but the page presents L/360 and L/240 pass labels from a single load as though they were general code checks.

Deflection alone does not establish member adequacy; bending, shear, bearing, buckling, connections, stability, vibration, creep, load combinations, self-weight, and material/code conditions are omitted despite sizing-oriented wording.

Imperial modulus is labeled ksi while presets/field values are psi; unit switching changes labels without converting or clearing values, and non-finite/large-deflection cases are not robustly rejected.
References: 2024 International Building Code Chapter 16 and American Wood Council calculator guidance.
Quarantine: ages 1-19 are incorrectly evaluated with adult BMI thresholds; pediatric interpretation requires age- and sex-specific percentiles, while adult categories apply at age 20 and older.
Imperial healthy-weight output calculates kilograms but labels pounds (70 in reports 58.5-78.7 lb instead of approximately 128.9-173.5 lb); body-fat and lean-mass labels are reversed.

BMR/TDEE energy is labeled cal rather than estimated kcal/day; the page gives automatic 20% intake advice, silently clamps body-fat estimates, and lacks finite/cross-field validation (including NaN/Infinity cases).
Unit switching changes labels without converting or clearing values. References: CDC BMI FAQ and U.S. Navy Guide 4 Body Composition Assessment.

Rechecked after correction: this is now explicitly a mean-cycle educational estimate, validates dates from 1900 through 2100 and fixed offsets from UTC-12 through UTC+14, and formats events in the selected offset instead of the browser timezone.

Residual limitation: sampled 2026 events differ from USNO ephemerides by as much as about 17.6 hours; a fixed offset does not model daylight saving time. Do not use for navigation, tides, eclipses, or precise observation.
Reference and benchmark: U.S. Naval Observatory moon-phases data/API.
Quarantine: solar declination is converted from degrees to radians twice, producing materially wrong sunrise, sunset, and day-length results.
Date-only parsing depends on the browser timezone; polar day/night yields NaN; coordinates, UTC offset, and date lack strict validation; time formatting can emit an impossible :60 minute.

The model uses a geometric horizon rather than the standard apparent-sunrise zenith and omits refraction/solar-disc assumptions. A New York 2026-06-21 fixture is roughly three hours short in daylight.
Manual fixed offsets omit DST and some quarter-hour zones. Reference: NOAA Solar Calculation Details and equations.
Quarantine: Web Speech recognition may delegate audio processing to a browser/vendor network service, contradicting the page and global catalog claim that inputs are always browser-local.
Relisting requires explicit pre-use disclosure/consent and capability-aware trust metadata, or a demonstrably local recognition implementation.
Quarantine: Web Speech synthesis can use network-backed voices that may transmit entered text, so the page cannot guarantee its 100% client-side claim.
Relisting requires explicit capability-aware disclosure and consent for browser-mediated services, or a demonstrably local synthesis implementation.
Quarantine: the selected source timezone is never used; datetime-local is parsed in the browser timezone, so conversion is wrong whenever the browser zone differs from the selected source.
DST gaps and repeated local times are not handled or disclosed, and the default local datetime is also wrong outside UTC.
The page needs a tested timezone-aware parser such as Temporal plus an explicit gap/fold policy, bounded validation, and accessible labels/live output. Reference: MDN datetime-local documentation.

Critical quarantine: safe conductor sizing cannot be determined from current, length, and voltage alone; material, insulation/terminal rating, installation method, ambient/grouping, continuous load, phase, jurisdiction, and allowable voltage drop are absent.

The ampacity/resistance table mixes assumptions and duplicates AWG 0; the second AWG 0 resistance resembles 3/0 while retaining a 1/0-style ampacity. A load above the table maximum still returns the undersized last row.
Length and voltage drop do not affect the selected gauge: the page can recommend AWG 14 for 15 A, 120 V, 100 m while reporting about 20.7% drop. Invalid edits can leave a stale recommendation.
The voltage-drop model assumes copper DC resistance and a two-wire round trip without saying so. References: Southwire voltage-drop calculator guidance and Cerrowire ampacity tables.
